text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police force report says 18 gangs of organised criminals were unveiled in 1996.
- President Suleyman Demirel sends letter to prime ministers of 15 European Union member states asking them not to exclude Turkey from Europe.
- The parliamentary immunity of former interior minister who resigned over security scandal might be lifted. He allegedly gave false police identity document to late gangster.
- Demirel says he has handed to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan information on the scandal given to him by main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz.
- A parliamentary commission rejects allegations of misdeeds by businessman seen as Islamist Welfare Party's financier.
- Three students wounded in far-rightist attacks at universities.
- Russia and Greece complain about Turkey in Black Sea economic cooperation meeting.
- Demirel asks for police special teams allegedly involved in political killings to be monitored.
- Military hospital reports reveal serious psychological problems suffered by soldiers fighting Kurdish rebels in southeast.
